summary:
Astro Jr. is a browser-based 3D game for kids ages 7–12. We developed a mission simulator where players control a junior astronaut walking around a fully explorable outpost on Mars (Jezero Crater) or the Moon (Shackleton Rim), built with Three.js — no download, no install, no account. Over 12 sols, players visit real stations: a power console for budgeting limited solar energy, a comm dish receiving Houston's orders, a greenhouse, lab, storm shelter, rover, and an ice deposit. Every task has a visible cost, so no choice is ever free.
The challenge asks us to teach real engineering trade-offs through play. Our game does this by grounding everything in genuine NASA data: the mission calendar maps to real days of DONKI space weather, so radiation storms, radio blackouts, and EVA restrictions come from actual CME speeds and SEP events. Radiation doses use real measurements (Curiosity RAD, Chang'e-4), and health facts link to real OSDR studies.
It's important because space education is usually abstract posters, not decisions. By letting kids physically feel "power spent on science is power not spent on oxygen," they internalize the trade-off logic mission planners face daily — turning real constraints into memorable, replayable gameplay.
details: A 3D space game for kids age 7-12 that micmics real life events using NASA datasets and apis to achieve that goal. Users must complete tasks risking tradeoffs.
